To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the continuous cold start problem is a significant problem in e-commerce applications; (2) contextual profiles can be constructed at scale from transaction logs; (3) contextual ranking can be used in real world applications with negligible CPU and RAM footprint; (4) contextual ranking improves user engagement in a real world online A/B test.
(1) the CoCoS problem is real and (2) it can be solved by leveraging contextual data from transaction logs to build contextual profiles that are useful in a real-world e-commerce application.

(i) the CoCoS Problem is a major issue in e-commerce, (ii) it can be solved by creating contextual profiles from implicit contextual cues from user transaction logs at scale and (iii) the resulting profiles can improve user engagement substantially.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of problems in recommender systems that are relevant to the e-commerce industry.
solving the Continuous Cold Start problem in e-commerce.
the problem of personalization in e-commerce applications where the user history is sparse and noisy and the situational context is implicit and not available.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can use contextual data from transaction logs in a scalable manner to solve the CoCoS problem and improve the user experience.
, in a real world e-commerce application, the continuous cold start problem can be solved by using contextual data to build contextual user profiles that can be used to improve the ranking.
contextual profiles are an effective way to personalize search results for users without a history, even in the absence of explicit situational context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show how the large scale availability and the sparsity of user interactions can be used to build a meaningful profile of users and their needs, which is useful to personalize the ranking of search results.
, even when the user history is not available, we can still build meaningful profiles from contextual data and that these profiles are useful to personalize the ranking.
, in e-commerce, we can solve the Continuous Cold Start problem with contextual ranking.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of explicit situational context, implicit cues in the transaction logs can be used to create contextual user profiles, and that these profiles can be used to improve user experience in real world e-commerce applications.
, when the history of a user is not available or too noisy to be useful, contextual user profiling is a viable alternative.
, in the absence of explicit situational context, the large scale of implicit data can be used to create meaningful user profiles that can be used to improve the quality of the recommendations.
